claim.operational_target: Test whether a noise-corrected anisotropic population covariance improves held-out synthetic-person logistic MAP NLL over the fixed isotropic personal MAP baseline.
non_claims: Covariance axes are beliefs, values, personality, or cognitive mechanisms.
Synthetic improvement transfers to real people.
alternatives: Fixed isotropic personal MAP is sufficient.
Estimated covariance is meta-person sampling noise.
Any gain is validation/test leakage or wrong-person support.
Linear-family gain disappears under stable misspecification.
claim.scope: Synthetic unseen people, one five-feature binary-choice task, support sizes 0/16/32/64, scenario confirmation, temporal secondary check, OOD diagnostic only.

identifiability.distinguishing_evidence: Previously unseen audit seeds, disjoint person roles, support-only adaptation, wrong-person EB control, null heterogeneity, and stable nonlinear misspecification control.
unidentified_questions: Whether the upstream collector disclosed every trial.

evidence.completeness_boundary: Synthetic generator completeness only; real evidence requires an external registry and trusted chronology.

computation.deployment_kernel: Anisotropic MAP produces a LogisticChoiceModel and all reporting uses LogisticChoiceModel.probabilities.
computation.selection_kernel: Validation selects only one fixed covariance-shrinkage coefficient from 0/.25/.5/.75/1.
computation.uncertainty_scope: Five-seed paired NLL audit plus null and misspecification controls; no real-person interval.

results.summary: 17/17 focused empirical-Bayes tests passed in 21.079s after hostile-audit repair.
Gate audit is expected to refuse confirmatory status: the module is exploratory and lacks real future holdout, global/local applicability, and temporal expiry evidence.

remaining_limitations: No real trial registry, trusted timestamps, or external signature.
Real-person applicability and expiry are not established.
Candidate must be rejected if preregistered comparative gates fail.
